message.content:
**Proteins that are commonly found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Typical Function | Representative Examples | |----------|------------------|------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often serve as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** such as β‑adrenergic receptor, rhodopsin
• **Ion channels**: voltage‑gated K⁺ channel (Kv), calcium channel (Cav), ligand‑gated NMDA receptor
• **Receptor tyrosine kinases**: EGFR, HER2
• **Integrins** (αβ heterodimers, e.g., α5β1)
• **Cadherins** (E‑cadherin, N‑cadherin)
• **Connexins** (gap‑junction hemichannels, e.g., Cx43)
• **Tetraspanins** (CD9, CD81) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via electrostatic or lipid‑anchor interactions; often link to cytoskeleton or signaling complexes. | • **Ankyrin‑R** (links integral proteins to spectrin)
• **Spectrin** (provides membrane skeleton)
• **Actin‑binding proteins**: ezrin, radixin, moesin (ERM family)
• **Src family kinases** (e.g., Src, Fyn) – attach via SH2/SH3 domains and lipid anchors
• **GAPs and GEFs** that regulate small GTPases at the membrane (e.g., p120‑RasGAP)
• **Adaptor proteins**: Grb2, Shc, LAT (link receptors to downstream pathways) | | **Lipid‑anchored proteins** | Covalently attached to membrane lipids (e.g., farnesyl, geranylgeranyl, palmitoyl). | • **H-Ras, K-Ras, N-Ras** (small GTPases)
• **GPI‑anchored proteins**: CD59, Thy-1, prion protein (PrP^C) | | **Other specialized proteins** | Involved in cell–cell communication, adhesion, or immune recognition. | • **MHC class I & II molecules** (antigen presentation)
• **Toll‑like receptors** (TLR4, TLR2)
• **Neurotransmitter receptors**: AMPA, NMDA, GABA_A, glycine receptor | ### How to think about plasma‑membrane proteins 1. **Transmembrane vs. peripheral** – Transmembrane proteins cross the bilayer; peripheral proteins sit on the inner or outer leaflet. 2. **Functional classes** – Channels, transporters, receptors, adhesion molecules, enzymes, scaffolds, and signaling adaptors. 3. **Structural motifs** – α‑helical transmembrane segments, β‑barrels (e.g., porins), lipid‑anchor motifs (C‑terminal CAAX box, GPI signal peptide). These proteins together give the plasma membrane its dynamic properties: selective permeability, signal transduction, cell adhesion, and structural integrity.

Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors, integrins, cadherins, connexins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins like ankyrin, spectrin, actin-binding proteins.
